Subject: Dedicated capacity expansion — post-renewal acceptance criteria & load-test plan

Hi Adam,

Thanks again for completing the renewal — excited to get the expanded Dedicated pools into steady state for Finlytics. Per the signed order (D-2025-9482) we’ve provisioned:

- Two reserved pools (prod-pool-A, prod-pool-B)
- Total: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (previously 8)
- Throughput target (contracted): 200 requests/min sustained per shard, with 2x burst capacity for 90s

Before we flip the final billing milestone, our standard acceptance asks for a short, supervised load run and a quick sign-off that latency/throughput meet the agreed SLOs. Proposed plan:

1) Load test window: Fri, Jan 17 — 09:00–11:00 PST (we’ll seed traffic from 3 regions)
2) Test cases: steady-state baseline (200 rpm), burst window (400 rpm for 90s), cold-start ramp
3) Success criteria (please confirm):
   - p95 latency < 250ms for generation paths used in your core pipeline
   - sustained throughput >= 200 rpm per shard for 10+ minutes without errors
   - error rate < 0.5% (5xx and timeouts)
4) Deliverables: PDF test report + raw traces, short runbook for ongoing monitoring

I attached a short test plan (redwood_dedicated_load_test_plan_20260116.pdf). Can you confirm the acceptance criteria above or list any additional checks (e.g., KV-cache hit-rate thresholds, tail-latency windows) you want us to include?

If that timeline looks good I’ll loop in Dylan to run and provide results and Marissa to coordinate billing/final paperwork.

Best,
Rafael

Subject: Load test results — Dedicated expansion (Finlytics)

Hi all,

Ran the scheduled load tests (see attached PDF and raw traces in the Drive link). High-level summary:

- Steady-state test (200 rpm per shard, 20 min):
  - sustained throughput: 210–225 rpm per shard
  - p95 latency (generation paths): 128ms
  - KV-cache hit rate: 87% (meets >85% target)
  - error rate: 0.22% (mostly transient 504s during a brief network blip at 09:32)
- Burst window (400 rpm for 90s):
  - peak throughput observed: 410 rpm total across pools
  - p99 during burst: 680ms (within the <750ms request)
  - no persistent OOMs or GPU crashes; GPU util avg 78% during burst
- Cold-start ramp: sub-second cold-starts for cached models; first-token latency for large model ~340ms

Action items / notes:
- We captured traces for the transient 504s — root cause appears to be a brief NAT gateway saturation in the test harness (not Redwood runtime). We recommend re-running the short steady-state test during a maintenance window if Finlytics wants a second verification.
- I pushed the summary PDF to Drive: https://redwood.app/drive/finlytics/load-tests/2026-01-17 (load_test_results_20260117.pdf).

Attachments: load_test_results_20260117.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Let me know if you want additional metrics (cold cache p95, token-by-token latency) — happy to run another targeted test.

Hi Adam — great to see the successful run and sign-off. Next operational steps from CS/ops:

- Billing: Marissa will confirm the final invoice and the committed capacity start date (expected billing transition: 2026-02-01).
- Monitoring baseline: we’ll enable the Finlytics dashboard in Redwood Console with the following alerts (suggested thresholds):
  - error rate > 0.5% (page to on-call)
  - p95 latency > 300ms for >5m (warning)
  - p99 latency > 800ms (page)
  - KV-cache hit-rate < 80% for 10m (warning)
- Runbook snippet (first 24 hours):
  1) If error rate spikes >0.5%: switch traffic to fallback model version, escalate to Redwood SE and Finlytics SRE.
  2) If sustained p99 > 800ms: open priority ticket, optionally scale up burst pool by 2 GPUs for immediate relief (requires approval).

We’ll schedule a 30-day check-in (Feb 17) to review telemetry and optimization opportunities (quantization, batching tweaks, route-level caches). Rafael / Marissa — can you confirm if Finlytics wants automated weekly reports (PDF) or just console access?
